about.title: About AssureProof
about.checks.1: AssureProof reads every document and keeps each figure tied to its source page. A language model then writes the draft. A formal consistency checker then tests whether the draft's figures and the values locked from the source can all be true at the same time. For a labeled figure, the language model does not make that call. For a sentence with no label, the language model turns it into a numeric comparison, and the formal consistency checker tests whether it holds. When a file is first read, the formal consistency checker can also flag figures in that file that contradict each other.

about.what.body: AssureProof is a platform that checks a draft against the files it was written from, before you pay or sign off. If an invoice is over the contract cap, or a claim doesn't match the policy, you see the mismatch on the review screen with both source pages open. A person decides whether each flagged figure is right. Fields read with high confidence that raise no Z3 or Red-Hat review objection can be accepted automatically, and that is recorded as an automatic accept. AssureProof runs inside your own environment.

security.title: Where AssureProof runs and what it stores
security.sub: AssureProof runs in your own AWS account, on a private GPU or on your own servers, including air-gapped networks. With a self-hosted model, document text stays inside your environment. Files are stored on your own disk or in your S3 bucket.
security.pillar1.title: Self-hosted or air-gapped
security.pillar1.desc: Deploy in your AWS VPC, on a private GPU cluster or in your own data center. Choose Amazon Bedrock in your account or a self-hosted model; with a self-hosted model, document text does not leave your network.
security.pillar2.title: No training on your documents
security.pillar2.desc: We do not use your documents to train models. Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.3 and at rest with AES-256, and you can use your own encryption keys (BYOK).
security.pillar3.title: A record of who decided what
security.pillar3.desc: Each accept, correction and dispute is logged with who, when, the old and new value and the reason. Field exports in JSON carry a signature you can verify, and CrossSure exports come with signed, chained receipts.
